name: Ultimaker S5
summary: A purpose-built desktop FDM printer: cartesian XY gantry with a Z-lifting bed, dual swappable print cores, and a Marlin-derived controller driven by standard G-code.

modelConstraints.sourceNote: Build volume 330 x 240 x 300 mm and 2.85 mm filament diameter are confirmed against Ultimaker's own published S5 specification sheet (https://ultimaker.com/3d-printers/s-series/ultimaker-s5/ and the linked PDF datasheet). axisCount/motionPrimitives are DOC-CONFIRMED against Marlin's G-code reference (https://marlinfw.org/meta/gcode/), since Ultimaker's firmware is a Marlin fork — not yet cross-checked against a real exported file from this specific unit's firmware build. reachMm/ratedPayloadG don't apply to this machine class the way they do to an arm and are left null.

evidence.label: DOC-CONFIRMED
evidence.scope: Layer-by-layer XY motion at a fixed Z is the foundational primitive of any Marlin-family FDM controller; not specific to this unit.

evidence.label: DOC-CONFIRMED
evidence.scope: Standard G1 E-axis moves plus M82/M83 extruder mode selection; universal across Marlin-family firmware.

evidence.label: DOC-CONFIRMED
evidence.scope: A single G1 command natively carries simultaneous X/Y/Z/E targets on any Marlin-family controller — unlike the Dobot reference machine, this isn't a repurposed use of a motion primitive designed for something else, it's what FDM G-code always does. This label covers the motion primitive existing and being well-documented, not that a specific non-planar surface has been print-tested on this unit; treat any specific slope/print-quality claim as a separate, unconfirmed question until a real print says otherwise.

installedTooling.name: Dual swappable print cores
installedTooling.description: The S5 ships with two independently-heated print cores (tool changer, not a mixing head). SAAM's post-processor for this machine currently targets single-extrusion output only (print core 1) — see postprocessor/README.md's known limitations. Dual-material/tool-change sequencing is deliberately out of scope for now, matching ROADMAP.md's Multi-material/multi-tool category, which isn't built yet.

safetyNotes: This is a fully enclosed, purpose-built desktop FDM printer, not a repurposed motion platform — most of the physical-safety caution that applies to the Dobot reference install (tool-load tuning, frame drift) doesn't apply here. The safety-relevant risk for this machine is in the G-code itself: a wrong extrusion-mode assumption (relative vs absolute E) or a wrong filament-diameter constant silently produces under- or over-extrusion rather than a visible fault.

Treat any exported file as unverified until confirmed against this unit's own accepted G-code conventions — see the post-processor's README for exactly what's been checked against a real exported/printed file versus what's still DOC-CONFIRMED only.
